name: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
authors: Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao (Princeton University + Google Brain/Research; work during Yao's Google internship)
reflection_type: none (substrate-level; ReAct itself has no explicit self-critique/reflection loop — it interleaves chain-of-thought 'thoughts' with environment-grounded actions/observations. It is the acting+reasoning substrate that later reflection methods such as Reflexion build on, not a reflection method per se)
feedback_source: external-tool / environment (observations returned by a Wikipedia search-and-lookup API for QA/Fever, and by interactive environments ALFWorld and WebShop). Thoughts are self-generated and not externally verified; the only feedback is the raw observation grounding from the environment.
iteration_structure: single-shot trajectory generation: an interleaved thought->action->observation loop generated greedily within a single episode (no episodic retry-with-reset, no tree/MCTS search, no population). For QA/Fever a fixed step budget (7 steps HotpotQA, 5 steps Fever) is used, after which it backs off to CoT-SC.
reflection_object: action trajectory and reasoning chain: ReAct interleaves free-form reasoning 'thoughts' (used to decompose questions, track progress, handle exceptions, reformulate searches, synthesize answers) with task-specific actions and grounds them in observations. The reflected/modified object is the in-flight action plan + working memory expressed in language, not the model weights or a persistent artifact.
learning_locus: in_context_verbal (primary contribution is few-shot in-context prompting with no weight update; the paper additionally explores an optional fine-tuning/bootstrapping variant on PaLM-8B/62B as a secondary experiment)
requires_training: none for the main method (few-shot prompting). Optional secondary experiment uses SFT (bootstrapping ~3,000 ReAct-generated correct trajectories à la STaR to finetune smaller PaLM-8B/62B models).
reward_or_critic_model: none (no reward model or learned critic; correctness is judged only by the task environment/oracle for evaluation, and during a trajectory the model relies on self-generated thoughts plus tool observations)
distillation_target: model-weights (only in the optional secondary experiment, where successful ReAct trajectories are bootstrapped and distilled via SFT into smaller PaLM models so they decode thoughts+actions+observations). The main method distills nothing — no reusable episodic memory, skill library, or rules.
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: the thought-action-observation interleaving is hand-designed via few-shot exemplars (human annotators type thoughts on top of actions), not an RL-emergent behavior. It predates and contrasts with RL-emergent reflection (e.g. DeepSeek-R1 'aha').
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad: the growing thought-action-observation context within the current episode acts as a working memory; there is no long-term episodic store, skill library, or playbook.
memory_persistence: within-episode (the trajectory context persists only for the current task instance; nothing is carried across episodes, tasks, or sessions)
memory_curation_mechanism: append-only (the trajectory grows by appending each thought/action/observation; bounded only by the LLM context-window limit and the per-task step budget. No summarization, Pareto selection, or overwrite/eviction is performed)
error_localization_granularity: step-level: reasoning is interleaved at each action step so the model can adjust the plan or reformulate a search mid-trajectory, but there is no explicit error attribution to a specific failing step (the paper analyzes failure modes holistically post-hoc by human labeling, not via algorithmic localization)
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task: reasoning and acting refine the plan within a single task instance; no experience is transferred across tasks (unlike Reflexion/ExpeL). The optional fine-tuning variant does generalize learned behavior across instances but is a separate experiment.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery: thoughts let the model handle exceptions, update plans, and reformulate searches in-flight within one episode; there is no cross-episode avoidance/retry mechanism in ReAct itself.
task_domains: QA/reasoning (multi-hop QA, fact verification), tool-use (Wikipedia search/lookup/finish API), web-navigation (online shopping), embodied/decision-making (text-based household tasks)
benchmarks: HotpotQA (multi-hop QA), FEVER (fact verification), ALFWorld (text-based embodied tasks, 134 unseen eval games), WebShop (online shopping, 500 test instructions)
headline_result: On two interactive decision-making benchmarks ReAct outperforms imitation- and reinforcement-learning baselines by an absolute success rate of +34% on ALFWorld and +10% on WebShop, while prompted with only 1-2 in-context examples. ReAct (best of 6) reaches 71% ALFWorld success vs Act 45% and BUTLER 37%; on WebShop ReAct scores 66.6 / 40.0% SR vs IL+RL 62.4 / 28.7%. On QA, combining ReAct with CoT-SC gives best results (HotpotQA EM 35.1 for ReAct->CoT-SC; Fever Acc 64.6 for CoT-SC->ReAct).
baselines: Standard prompting; Chain-of-Thought (CoT, Wei et al. 2022); CoT with self-consistency (CoT-SC, 21 samples); Act-only (no thoughts, WebGPT-like); ReAct-IM (Inner-Monologue-style dense external feedback ablation); for ALFWorld: BUTLER / BUTLERg imitation-learning agents; for WebShop: imitation learning (IL) and imitation+reinforcement learning (IL+RL) from Yao et al. 2022; supervised SoTA references for HotpotQA/Fever.
gains_vs_baseline: ALFWorld: ReAct best-of-6 71% vs best Act 45% (+26 pts absolute) and vs BUTLER 37% (+34 pts absolute, the headline 34%); ReAct's advantage over Act consistent across 6 trials (relative gain 33-90%, avg 62%); ReAct also beats the Inner-Monologue-style ReAct-IM ablation (71 vs 53). WebShop: ReAct SR 40.0% vs best IL+RL 28.7% (+~11 pts; headline ~10% absolute over prior best SR) and score 66.6 vs 62.4. QA (PaLM-540B): ReAct alone HotpotQA EM 27.4 (slightly below CoT 29.4 / CoT-SC 33.4) but Fever Acc 60.9 (above CoT 56.3); combined CoT-SC<->ReAct gives best EM 35.1 (HotpotQA) and Acc 64.6 (Fever), beating all prompting baselines. Human/expert and supervised SoTA (HotpotQA 67.5 / Fever 89.5) remain far higher.
compute_cost_profile: Higher inference cost than single-pass CoT: each task requires a multi-step thought-action-observation loop (multiple LLM calls plus external API/environment calls per episode); the QA combination method additionally samples 21 CoT-SC trajectories for the back-off. Few-shot only, so no training cost for the main method; the optional fine-tuning variant adds SFT cost on ~3,000 bootstrapped trajectories. The paper does not report an explicit token/API-call multiplier.
known_limitations: Complex tasks with large action spaces need more demonstrations than fit in the in-context window (input-length limit). The structural thought-action-observation constraint reduces reasoning flexibility, giving ReAct a higher reasoning-error rate than CoT on HotpotQA (47% of failures) and a distinctive failure mode of repetitively regenerating the same thoughts/actions (error loops, attributed to greedy decoding). It also suffers search-result errors (23% of HotpotQA failures) when the simple Wikipedia API returns empty/irrelevant passages. ReAct alone slightly underperforms CoT on HotpotQA. Hooking an LLM to real action spaces carries safety risks.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: external-tool/verifier (environment-dependent): ReAct's grounding comes from environment observations (Wikipedia API, ALFWorld/WebShop env), not from oracle labels during a trajectory. It does not use ground-truth answers to self-correct; thoughts are self-generated and unverified, so its 'reasoning' component is intrinsic while its factual grounding depends on the external tool/environment.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent: interleaving reasoning with grounded action is net-positive on grounded/interactive tasks (sharply cuts CoT's hallucination, 6% vs 14% false-positive rate; big gains on ALFWorld/WebShop and Fever) but ReAct's pure reasoning is more error-prone than CoT on HotpotQA. The strongest results come from combining ReAct with CoT-SC rather than either alone. Note ReAct is a substrate, not a self-correction method.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report confidence-calibration metrics; it analyzes hallucination/false-positive rates and success/failure-mode percentages rather than calibration)
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (ReAct is a method paper, not a failure-attribution study; it provides a manual human-labeled success/failure-mode breakdown of its own and CoT trajectories on HotpotQA but does not implement automatic failure attribution)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets/mitigates hallucination and error propagation in chain-of-thought (by grounding in external knowledge) and poor goal decomposition / loss of state tracking in action-only agents. Exposes its own characteristic failure modes: reasoning errors including error-loops (repetitive thought/action regeneration), search-result errors, and (relative to CoT) reduced reasoning flexibility. Maps loosely to MAST-style modes such as error-loops and (later-named) superficial/constrained self-reflection.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark released; ReAct uses existing benchmarks (HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, WebShop). The authors released prompts, GPT-3 ReAct prompting code, and the project page/repo (react-lm.github.io / github.com/ysymyth/ReAct).
builds_on: Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022) and self-consistency CoT-SC (Wang et al. 2022); Inner Monologue (Huang et al. 2022b) and Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners (Huang et al. 2022a) for LLM planning/acting; WebGPT (Nakano et al. 2021) for tool-augmented acting; STaR-style bootstrapping (Zelikman et al. 2022) for the fine-tuning variant; the WebShop (Yao et al. 2022) and ALFWorld (Shridhar et al. 2020) environments.
extended_by_or_inspired: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023; adds verbal self-reflection/episodic memory on top of a ReAct-style agent), Tree of Thoughts (Yao et al. 2023), Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023), ExpeL (cross-task experience), AutoGPT/BabyAGI and most tool-using/agent frameworks (LangChain ReAct agents), Toolformer-style tool use, Voyager, and the broad 2023-2026 LLM-agent literature that treats interleaved reason+act as the default substrate.
citation_count: ~7,158 (Semantic Scholar, Corpus ID 252762395, as of mid-2025; one of the most-cited LLM-agent papers)
reasoning_model_native: no / predates reasoning models: ReAct (2022) is a prompt-engineered scaffold for non-reasoning base LLMs (PaLM-540B, GPT-3). It is not native to o1/R1-style models that have built-in reflection, though the interleaved reason+act paradigm is often layered on top of such models in later work (tool-use agents).
on_policy_distillation_link: weak/indirect: the main method is in-context with no distillation. The optional secondary experiment bootstraps ReAct's own successful trajectories and SFT-distills them into smaller PaLM models (STaR-style on-policy self-generated data), an early conceptual precursor to on-policy distillation / agent-trajectory distillation, but it is offline SFT rather than true on-policy distillation.
sample_efficiency: Extremely few-shot: 1-2 in-context examples for ALFWorld/WebShop, 6 (HotpotQA) and 3 (Fever) exemplars for QA; the paper notes more examples do not improve performance. The optional fine-tuning variant uses ~3,000 bootstrapped trajectories.
